stages.name: Requirements
stages.entryQuestion: Before designing a notification platform, what scope and scale assumptions would you clarify?
stages.objective: Agree on product behavior, measurable quality targets and the stated exercise workload.

completionCriteria.name: Functional scope
completionCriteria.guidance: Clarify transactional versus bulk priority, selected channels, acceptance semantics and user preferences.

completionCriteria.name: Quality targets
completionCriteria.guidance: Separate durable API acceptance from provider acceptance and final delivery; define latency and retention for each.

completionCriteria.name: Capacity estimates
completionCriteria.guidance: Use the fictional baseline or state a justified alternative; derive average and peak rates and distinguish payload bytes from replication and indexes.

stages.name: High Level Design
stages.entryQuestion: Walk me through durable acceptance, routing and channel delivery.
stages.objective: Keep provider latency off the acceptance path and isolate channels.

completionCriteria.name: Durable acceptance
completionCriteria.guidance: Persist a stable intent ID and recoverable dispatch work before acknowledging; a transactional outbox or equivalent is acceptable.

completionCriteria.name: Routing and preferences
completionCriteria.guidance: Resolve recipients and allowed channels using current preferences, including quiet hours.

completionCriteria.name: Channel isolation
completionCriteria.guidance: Use bounded per-channel work and provider adapters with independent quotas and failure domains.

stages.name: Core Flow
stages.entryQuestion: How does a notification behave when a provider times out and the sender retries?
stages.objective: Explain identity, retry uncertainty and per-channel completion.

completionCriteria.name: Intent idempotency
completionCriteria.guidance: Scope a caller-provided key to its tenant and compare the request fingerprint so a retried intent is not duplicated.

completionCriteria.name: Attempt lifecycle
completionCriteria.guidance: Track pending, leased, attempted and terminal outcomes per channel; distinguish provider acceptance from confirmed delivery.

completionCriteria.name: Retry uncertainty
completionCriteria.guidance: Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter and provider idempotency keys when supported; acknowledge that an ambiguous timeout may still duplicate delivery.

completionCriteria.name: Eligibility at send time
completionCriteria.guidance: Recheck opt-out and quiet-hour policy before the actual attempt, not just when the intent is created.

stages.name: Data Model
stages.entryQuestion: What keys and tables would track notification intents, attempts, preferences and receipts?
stages.objective: Model durable state transitions and a bounded deduplication window.

completionCriteria.name: Intent schema
completionCriteria.guidance: Store tenant, intent ID, idempotency key, recipient reference, template version and request hash; protect sensitive parameters.

completionCriteria.name: Attempt schema
completionCriteria.guidance: Represent each channel/provider attempt with attempt number, lease expiry, retry time and provider reference.

completionCriteria.name: Preferences and receipts
completionCriteria.guidance: Version user preferences and deduplicate asynchronous provider receipts; enforce tenant isolation.

stages.name: Reliability
stages.entryQuestion: How would you handle provider outages, worker crashes, opt-outs and permanently invalid addresses?
stages.objective: Prevent endless retries and isolate degraded providers.

completionCriteria.name: Lease and replay
completionCriteria.guidance: Recover abandoned work from durable state and make completion idempotent after a worker crashes.

completionCriteria.name: Failure classification
completionCriteria.guidance: Retry transient errors, stop on permanent failures, dead-letter exhausted attempts and support controlled replay.

completionCriteria.name: Provider protection
completionCriteria.guidance: Respect provider quotas and retry delays, use circuit breaking, and avoid a fallback provider causing duplicate sends.

stages.name: Scaling
stages.entryQuestion: How would you handle a tenfold burst while one channel provider is throttling?
stages.objective: Scale worker pools and preserve priority under backpressure.

completionCriteria.name: Attempt capacity
completionCriteria.guidance: Derive 231.48 intents/s and 347.22 channel attempts/s average, with 3472.22 peak attempts/s before retries.

completionCriteria.name: Queue partitioning
completionCriteria.guidance: Partition by channel and tenant or priority; prevent one bulk campaign from starving transactional traffic.

completionCriteria.name: Storage budget
completionCriteria.guidance: Estimate 140 GB of 7-day raw intent records and 420 GB with three copies, before indexes and individual attempt rows.

stages.name: Tradeoffs
stages.entryQuestion: Which delivery guarantees and cost tradeoffs would you expose to callers?
stages.objective: Explain practical provider and product boundaries.

completionCriteria.name: Guarantee tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Explain at-least-once internal processing versus best-effort external deduplication; do not promise universal exactly-once sends.

completionCriteria.name: Latency tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Compare immediate transactional delivery with scheduled or bulk work under provider cost and quota limits.

completionCriteria.name: Privacy and operations
concepts: Queue age and provider error metrics
completionCriteria.guidance: Minimize retention and payload logging; monitor oldest queued age, terminal failures and provider throttles without recipient labels.
